subtopics.title: The Code in maternity practice: the four themes
subtopics.blurb: Use the four themes of the NMC Code to decide what a midwife should do for a woman and her baby.

subtopics.title: Registration, revalidation and fitness to practise
subtopics.blurb: Know exactly what a midwife needs to revalidate every three years, and how the NMC acts when fitness to practise is in question.

subtopics.title: The role and scope of the autonomous midwife
subtopics.blurb: Explain the midwife's role as accountable lead professional, its legal limits, and what happens when care needs an obstetrician.

subtopics.title: Partnership, communication and person-centred relationships
subtopics.blurb: Work in partnership with women, involve partners and family on her terms, and use independent interpreters well.

subtopics.title: Record keeping, numeracy and digital literacy
subtopics.blurb: Keep maternity records that are contemporaneous, accurate and secure, and use numeracy and digital skills safely.

subtopics.title: Candour, raising concerns and escalation
subtopics.blurb: Be open with women when things go wrong, know the statutory duty of candour, and raise and escalate concerns effectively.

subtopics.title: Professional judgement and influences on decisions
subtopics.blurb: Explain the reasoning behind your decisions, spot personal and external influences, and keep professional boundaries.

subtopics.title: Legal and regulatory frameworks across the four UK nations
subtopics.blurb: Tell statute from case law and guidance, know which regulator covers what in each UK nation, and meet midwives' mandatory reporting duties.

subtopics.title: Human rights and sexual and reproductive rights
subtopics.blurb: Apply the Human Rights Act 1998 to childbirth: autonomy, dignity, privacy and women's choices about birth and reproduction.

subtopics.title: Informed consent and material risk (Montgomery)
subtopics.blurb: Seek valid consent from women for themselves and their newborns, disclosing material risks and reasonable alternatives as Montgomery requires.

subtopics.title: Declining care and choices outside guidance
subtopics.blurb: Respect a competent woman's right to decline, even when her baby's life is at stake, and keep caring and advocating when her choices are outside guidance.

subtopics.title: Mental capacity in pregnancy and labour
subtopics.blurb: Apply the Mental Capacity Act 2005 to decisions in pregnancy and labour: presume capacity, support decisions, assess properly and act in best interests.

subtopics.title: Confidentiality and information sharing
subtopics.blurb: Protect what a woman tells you, let her control who is told, and share purposefully when safety demands it.

subtopics.title: Termination of pregnancy and related law
subtopics.blurb: Know the lawful grounds for termination across the UK and exactly what conscientious objection does and does not cover.

subtopics.title: Equality, anti-racism and advocacy for women made vulnerable
subtopics.blurb: Apply the Equality Act, read the inequality data, and advocate for women whose care is at risk of being unequal.

subtopics.title: Continuity of care and carer
subtopics.blurb: Explain what continuity of carer is, what the current evidence shows, and how national policy now targets it safely.

subtopics.title: Organising maternity services and national policy
subtopics.blurb: Map the settings, lead professionals and system structures of maternity care, and spot the staffing red flags that threaten safety.

subtopics.title: Planning place of birth
subtopics.blurb: Give women the NICE NG235 evidence on each birth setting, for first and later babies, and support the choice they make.

subtopics.title: Social context and women who find services hard to reach
subtopics.blurb: Recognise complex social factors, treat late booking as a signal, and adapt care with other agencies so every woman can reach it.

subtopics.title: Keeping the needs of woman and baby together
subtopics.blurb: Plan care for the woman and her newborn as one unit, avoid needless separation, and keep them connected when they must be apart.

subtopics.title: Coordinating care and transfer of care
subtopics.blurb: Act as coordinator of care: transfer safely in labour, hand over with the woman at the centre, and pass care seamlessly to the health visitor and GP.

subtopics.title: Protecting breastfeeding in all settings
subtopics.blurb: Know the law on breastfeeding in public, work within the WHO Code, and team up with agencies and communities to protect breastfeeding.

subtopics.title: The midwife's public health role and epidemiology
subtopics.blurb: Read maternity data accurately, explain risk in numbers women understand, and use every contact to protect lifelong health.

subtopics.title: Preconception health, nutrition and supplements
subtopics.blurb: Give current NICE NG247 advice on folic acid, vitamin D, weight, Healthy Start and food safety before and during pregnancy.

subtopics.title: Smoking, alcohol and substance use
subtopics.blurb: Test CO, make the opt-out referral, give clear alcohol advice and open the right pathway when a woman discloses substance use.

subtopics.title: Immunisation in pregnancy
subtopics.blurb: Time pertussis, RSV and flu vaccines correctly in every pregnancy, and explain why live vaccines usually wait until after the birth.

subtopics.title: Infection prevention, antimicrobial stewardship and infectious disease screening
subtopics.blurb: Apply hand hygiene and standard precautions, use antibiotics wisely, run IDPS screening and act on GBS when the waters break.

subtopics.title: Sexual and reproductive health and contraception
subtopics.blurb: Advise on when fertility returns, which methods can start straight after birth, when combined methods are safe, and when breastfeeding counts as contraception.

subtopics.title: Domestic abuse, FGM and safeguarding
subtopics.blurb: Ask about domestic abuse safely, respond to disclosure, apply the FGM reporting duty correctly and share information under the 2026 duty.

subtopics.title: Parent education, attachment and safe sleep
subtopics.blurb: Prepare parents for birth and parenthood, promote attachment, advise on going-to-sleep position in pregnancy and give safe infant sleep advice, including bed-sharing.

subtopics.title: Human milk, breastfeeding and Baby Friendly
subtopics.blurb: Explain why breastfeeding matters to public health, apply UNICEF UK Baby Friendly standards and support an informed feeding choice, including safe formula feeding.

subtopics.title: Anatomy, physiology and genetics of pregnancy and fetal development
subtopics.blurb: Explain the normal changes of pregnancy in each body system, trace the fetal circulation and its shunts, and use basic genetics to explain screening.

subtopics.title: The booking appointment
subtopics.blurb: Book by 10+0 weeks, take a full history, carry out the booking measurements and bloods, offer screening and complete the risk assessments that shape the whole pregnancy.

subtopics.title: Antenatal schedule and ongoing assessment
subtopics.blurb: Plan 10 or 7 appointments by parity, know what happens at each contact, measure and plot fundal height, and check presentation from 36 weeks.

subtopics.title: Antenatal screening programmes and ethical choices
subtopics.blurb: Time and explain the FASP, SCT and IDPS tests, interpret a higher-chance result, describe NIPT and diagnostic options, and support a free, informed choice.

subtopics.title: Blood pressure, proteinuria and pre-eclampsia risk
subtopics.blurb: Measure and act on blood pressure and proteinuria at every visit, classify hypertension in pregnancy, and identify who needs aspirin from 12 weeks.

subtopics.title: Fetal growth and fetal movements
subtopics.blurb: Measure and plot fundal height to Saving Babies' Lives v3, and manage reduced fetal movements with the ask, act, advise checklist.

subtopics.title: Blood group, antibodies and anti-D
subtopics.blurb: Use blood group and antibody results to protect RhD-negative women and their babies: routine prophylaxis, sensitising events and care after birth.

subtopics.title: Psychological change and mental health enquiry
subtopics.blurb: Ask the Whooley and GAD-2 questions well, act on the answers, and recognise who needs specialist perinatal mental health care.

subtopics.title: Prolonged pregnancy, membrane sweep and induction
subtopics.blurb: Support informed decisions about sweeps and induction under NICE NG207, choose the method from the Bishop score, and care for women who decline.

subtopics.title: Common symptoms of pregnancy
subtopics.blurb: Give evidence-based advice for nausea, heartburn, constipation, pelvic girdle pain and varicose veins, and spot the symptoms that are not normal.

subtopics.title: Physiology and mechanisms of labour
subtopics.blurb: Explain how contractions build, define each stage of labour, and follow the baby's journey through the pelvis.

subtopics.title: Latent labour, early assessment and prelabour rupture of membranes
subtopics.blurb: Triage and support women in latent labour, and manage prelabour rupture of membranes at term under NICE NG235.

subtopics.title: Monitoring progress and delay in labour
subtopics.blurb: Record first-stage observations on a partogram, recognise transfer triggers, and manage delay in the first and second stages under NICE NG235.

subtopics.title: Intermittent auscultation and CTG interpretation
subtopics.blurb: Listen in correctly with intermittent auscultation, categorise CTG features as white, amber or red, and act on the overall picture under NICE NG229.

subtopics.title: Pain relief in labour
subtopics.blurb: Give accurate information on every option from breathing to epidural, and provide safe care and observations for each under NICE NG235.

subtopics.title: Optimising physiological birth and the birth environment
subtopics.blurb: Create an environment and give the one-to-one, low-intervention care that supports physiological labour, including position, hydration and bladder care.

subtopics.title: Second stage, perineal care and trauma classification
subtopics.blurb: Support pushing and protect the perineum in the second stage, classify perineal trauma correctly, and carry out a systematic assessment after birth.

subtopics.title: Third stage of labour and cord clamping
subtopics.blurb: Explain active and physiological third stage, choose a safe uterotonic, time cord clamping and recognise a prolonged third stage under NICE NG235.

subtopics.title: Postnatal physiology and routine assessment
subtopics.blurb: Carry out the NICE NG194 postnatal check: involution and lochia, perineum, bladder and bowels, and the timing of each postnatal contact.

subtopics.title: Postnatal red flags and escalation
subtopics.blurb: Recognise the NICE NG194 warning symptoms after birth, link each to its likely cause, and escalate postnatal hypertension and suspected sepsis correctly.

subtopics.title: Venous thromboembolism risk
subtopics.blurb: Score VTE risk at booking, on admission and after birth using RCOG GTG 37a as amended in September 2026, and recognise when LMWH is needed and when a clot is suspected.

subtopics.title: Physiology of lactation and infant feeding
subtopics.blurb: Explain how milk is made and released, why colostrum and responsive feeding matter, and what feeding choices mean for the health of women and babies.

subtopics.title: Supporting breastfeeding and formula feeding
subtopics.blurb: Support positioning and attachment, assess a feed, advise on expressing and mastitis, and teach safe formula preparation and responsive bottle feeding (NICE NG194).

subtopics.title: Transition to parenthood and postnatal mental wellbeing
subtopics.blurb: Support bonding and the move into parenthood, tell baby blues from depression and psychosis, and use the Whooley and GAD-2 questions to decide when to refer (NICE CG192, NG194).

subtopics.title: Culturally sensitive and individualised care
subtopics.blurb: Give care shaped by the needs and preferences each woman identifies, use professional interpreters, avoid assumptions, and respond to health inequalities (NMC SPM, the Code, NICE).

subtopics.title: Transition to extrauterine life and immediate care
subtopics.blurb: Support a baby's transition at birth: Apgar scoring, skin-to-skin and warmth, the first feed, and observations after meconium or prolonged rupture of membranes (NICE NG235, RCUK 2025).

subtopics.title: Newborn and infant physical examination (NIPE)
subtopics.blurb: Explain the NIPE screen of eyes, heart, hips and testes, its timing (by 72 hours and at 6 to 8 weeks), hip risk factors and each screen-positive referral pathway.

subtopics.title: Newborn blood spot and hearing screening
subtopics.blurb: Offer the newborn blood spot test (day 5, 10 conditions) and the hearing screen, explain consent and declining rules, and know what happens after a no clear response result.

subtopics.title: Vitamin K prophylaxis
subtopics.blurb: Offer vitamin K to prevent vitamin K deficiency bleeding: IM as first choice, the oral regimens if parents prefer, doses from the BNFC, and consent (NICE NG235, reinstated 2026).

subtopics.title: Neonatal jaundice
subtopics.blurb: Spot the babies at risk, choose the right bilirubin test and time frame, care for a baby under phototherapy and act on prolonged jaundice (NICE CG98).

subtopics.title: Thermoregulation, hypoglycaemia and NEWTT2
subtopics.blurb: Keep a newborn warm, protect at-risk babies from hypoglycaemia and use NEWTT2, red flags and parents' concerns to escalate a baby who is becoming unwell.

subtopics.title: Newborn behaviour and very early child development
subtopics.blurb: Read a newborn's cues, support bonding and responsive feeding, track early weight and growth, and know what is checked at 6 to 8 weeks.

subtopics.title: Pharmacology across the continuum of care
subtopics.blurb: Apply pharmacokinetics, timing of exposure, allergies, contraindications, interactions and over-the-counter use to medicines for women and babies.

subtopics.title: Midwives exemptions, PGDs and controlled drugs
subtopics.blurb: Know which medicines midwives and student midwives may give under the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 Schedule 17, when a PGD or prescription is needed, and how controlled drugs are handled.

subtopics.title: Uterotonics and other obstetric medicines
subtopics.blurb: Use oxytocin, ergometrine, carboprost, misoprostol, tranexamic acid and magnesium sulfate safely: doses, contraindications, sequence and monitoring.

subtopics.title: Medicines in pregnancy and breastfeeding
subtopics.blurb: Recognise key teratogens (valproate, ACE inhibitors, lithium), support safe antihypertensive use with breastfeeding, and use reliable information sources.

subtopics.title: Safe administration and medicines errors
subtopics.blurb: Carry out the checks before every dose, avoid medication Never Events, respond openly to an error and report suspected adverse reactions through the Yellow Card scheme.

subtopics.title: Recognising deterioration and escalation tools
subtopics.blurb: Use maternity early warning scores, NICE NG255 sepsis criteria and SBAR to recognise a woman who is becoming unwell and escalate at the right speed.

subtopics.title: Postpartum haemorrhage
subtopics.blurb: Define and anticipate postpartum haemorrhage, take the NICE immediate actions, choose the right uterotonic and add tranexamic acid (NG235, RCOG GTG 52).

subtopics.title: Shoulder dystocia
subtopics.blurb: Recognise shoulder dystocia, call for help, start McRoberts and suprapubic pressure, avoid fundal pressure and non-axial traction, and document and follow up (RCOG GTG 42, 3rd edition).

subtopics.title: Umbilical cord prolapse
subtopics.blurb: Recognise cord prolapse, handle the cord minimally, relieve compression by elevating the presenting part or filling the bladder, position the woman safely and arrange the right category of birth (RCOG GTG 50).

subtopics.title: Severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia
subtopics.blurb: Recognise severe pre-eclampsia, give and monitor magnesium sulfate safely, control blood pressure and restrict fluids under NICE NG133.

subtopics.title: Maternal sepsis
subtopics.blurb: Grade suspected sepsis in pregnant and recently pregnant women with NICE NG255, act within the 1-hour targets and transfer safely from the community.

subtopics.title: Antepartum haemorrhage
subtopics.blurb: Tell placenta praevia from placental abruption, avoid a dangerous vaginal examination, give anti-D correctly and act first for the mother using RCOG GTG 63.

subtopics.title: Maternal collapse and resuscitation
subtopics.blurb: Lead the first minutes of a maternal cardiac arrest: call for help, high-quality CPR, manual uterine displacement, the 4Hs, 4Ts and 4Ps, and early preparation for resuscitative hysterotomy (RCUK 2025).

subtopics.title: Unexpected breech birth
subtopics.blurb: Recognise a breech in labour, support the woman's choice, keep hands off, know when and how to intervene, and get neonatal help ready (RCOG GTG 20b, NICE NG121).

subtopics.title: Newborn life support
subtopics.blurb: Support a newborn's transition and resuscitate using the RCUK 2025 algorithm: warmth, airway, inflation breaths at the right pressure and oxygen, ventilation, compressions at 3:1 and adrenaline.

subtopics.title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
subtopics.blurb: Classify chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia, and apply NICE NG133 on aspirin, labetalol, the 135/85 target, PlGF testing, timing of birth and postnatal care.

subtopics.title: Diabetes in pregnancy
subtopics.blurb: Screen for and diagnose gestational diabetes, apply NICE NG3 glucose targets and treatment steps, plan timing of birth and care for the baby after birth.

subtopics.title: Preterm labour and birth
subtopics.blurb: Apply NICE NG25 and Saving Babies' Lives v3 element 5: prevention with progesterone or cerclage, P-PROM, diagnosis by cervical length, tocolysis, steroids, magnesium for neuroprotection and the right place of birth.

subtopics.title: Fetal growth restriction and multiple pregnancy
subtopics.blurb: Risk-assess and monitor fetal growth with Saving Babies' Lives v3 element 2, act on a small baby, and understand chorionicity, scan schedules and timing of birth for twins and triplets (NICE NG137).

subtopics.title: Perinatal mental illness
subtopics.blurb: Ask the right questions, recognise severe mental illness and postpartum psychosis as an emergency, refer on time and support safe medicines and feeding (NICE CG192).

subtopics.title: Newborns needing additional care
subtopics.blurb: Keep mothers and babies together through transitional care, recognise early-onset neonatal infection with NICE NG195, manage low blood glucose and feeding problems, and escalate with NEWTT2.

subtopics.title: Social complexity and multiagency care
subtopics.blurb: Give women with complex social factors the extra, coordinated care NICE CG110 sets out, while you keep providing their midwifery care.

subtopics.title: Pregnancy loss, stillbirth and end of life care
subtopics.blurb: Offer the right birth options after an intrauterine death, give compassionate care to the National Bereavement Care Pathway standards, and explain how the baby's death will be reviewed.

subtopics.title: Human factors and multidisciplinary teamwork
subtopics.blurb: Explain why skilled midwives still make errors, match each error type to the fix that works, and use team training and shared awareness to keep women and babies safe.

subtopics.title: Escalation, handover and speaking up
subtopics.blurb: Escalate clearly with SBAR, keep going up the chain when a concern is not acted on, use fresh eyes on fetal monitoring, and raise concerns about public protection the right way.

subtopics.title: Incidents, investigation and learning
subtopics.blurb: Report near misses and incidents, know when MNSI investigates, meet the duty of candour, and share learning with families under PSIRF.

subtopics.title: Learning from national reports and data
subtopics.blurb: Use Ockenden, East Kent, MBRRACE-UK and Saving Babies' Lives v3 to explain what went wrong nationally and what midwives now do differently.

subtopics.title: Quality improvement, change and sustainable care
subtopics.blurb: Run a small PDSA test of change with the right measures, advocate for evidence-informed change, know the NHS net zero targets, and share data safely between teams.

subtopics.title: Safe staffing and skill mix
subtopics.blurb: Explain how staffing and skill mix affect safety, protect one-to-one care in labour, and act on NICE NG4 midwifery red flags.

subtopics.title: Team reflection and acting safely without evidence
subtopics.blurb: Lead or join a useful team debrief, reflect in a way that changes practice, and make safe, shared, documented decisions when the evidence is weak or missing.

subtopics.title: Wellbeing, vulnerability and resilience
subtopics.blurb: Notice when you or a colleague are struggling, act in a way that is kind and safe, and use restorative supervision and self-care to stay well in a demanding job.

subtopics.title: Research evidence and critical appraisal
subtopics.blurb: Match research questions to study designs, rank evidence, appraise a study critically, and explain risk to women in a way they can use.

subtopics.title: Audit, service evaluation and contributing to knowledge
subtopics.blurb: Tell audit, service evaluation and research apart using the HRA definitions, run a complete audit cycle, and involve women in shaping services.

subtopics.title: Leadership, prioritising and delegation
subtopics.blurb: Prioritise women and babies by acuity, delegate safely to maternity support workers under Code 11, and lead by example whatever your band.

subtopics.title: Supporting and supervising students
subtopics.blurb: Know the SSSA roles for student midwives, give feedback that helps, document performance properly, and keep students inside the law on medicines.

subtopics.title: Professional development and career pathways
subtopics.blurb: Plan CPD that meets revalidation, reflect and use feedback well, and map the career routes open to a midwife in practice, management, education, research and policy.

subtopics.title: Decimals and place value: moving the point, leading zeros and tenfold errors
subtopics.blurb: Read every digit's true value, move the decimal point the right number of places, and write doses so they cannot be misread tenfold.

subtopics.title: Mass conversions: kg, g, mg, micrograms and nanograms
subtopics.blurb: Convert confidently between kg, g, mg, micrograms and nanograms, knowing which way the point moves and why a mg/microgram slip is a thousandfold error.

subtopics.title: Volume conversions: L and mL
subtopics.blurb: Convert between litres and millilitres in both directions, add mixed volumes safely and type the answer in the unit the box asks for.

subtopics.title: Weights in grams and kilograms for babies and children
subtopics.blurb: Convert baby and child weights between grams and kilograms, round to two decimal places correctly and use the weight in kg for doses and feeds.

subtopics.title: Units, international units and millimoles on labels and prescriptions
subtopics.blurb: Work with doses in units and millimoles from the strength on the label, write "units" safely and enter the answer in the right box.

subtopics.title: Time: hours and minutes, the 24-hour clock and finish times
subtopics.blurb: Convert between hours and minutes, use the 24-hour clock, and work out infusion durations and finish times, including across midnight.

subtopics.title: Percentages, fractions and ratio strengths (% w/v, 1 in 1,000)
subtopics.blurb: Turn % w/v and "1 in" ratio strengths into grams, milligrams and micrograms per mL, and work out percentages of a dose.

subtopics.title: Reading a graduated syringe: scale intervals and where to read the plunger
subtopics.blurb: Work out what each small mark on any syringe is worth, read the volume at the right edge of the plunger seal and type it in Pearson format.

subtopics.title: Reading a medicine pot or oral measure
subtopics.blurb: Work out the scale on a medicine pot, read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level and record the volume dispensed in Pearson format.

subtopics.title: Choosing the right syringe or measure for the volume
subtopics.blurb: Pick the smallest syringe or measure that holds the whole dose and is marked finely enough to measure it exactly.

subtopics.title: The core formula: what you want over what you have, times the volume
subtopics.blurb: Use want ÷ have x volume for liquids and want ÷ have for tablets, with units matched first and rounding left to the end.

subtopics.title: Reading strengths from labels: mg/5 mL, mg in 1 mL, mg/2 mL, units/mL
subtopics.blurb: Read what a label's strength really means, find the amount per mL or per container, and pick the right numbers for want ÷ have.

subtopics.title: Number of tablets for a prescribed dose
subtopics.blurb: Work out how many tablets make one prescribed dose, check it makes sense, and type it the way Pearson marks it.

subtopics.title: Tablets when prescription and stock use different units (g, mg, micrograms)
subtopics.blurb: Convert the prescription and the stock into the same unit, then work out the tablets without a thousandfold slip.

subtopics.title: Half tablets: only when the stem says the tablet is scored
subtopics.blurb: Give half tablets when, and only when, the tablet is scored, and type answers such as 1.5 and 0.5 correctly.

subtopics.title: Daily totals from frequency: BD, TDS, QDS and hourly intervals
subtopics.blurb: Turn a dose and a frequency into a 24-hour total in mg, g or tablets without mixing up intervals and counts.

subtopics.title: Stock counts: tablets left, supply for N days, ampoules or nebules needed
subtopics.blurb: Work out tablets used, tablets left, how long a supply lasts and how many ampoules to open, rounding up where you must.

subtopics.title: Oral liquid volumes from mg/5 mL and mg/1 mL
subtopics.blurb: Calculate the volume of an oral liquid from its label strength, including the stock volume, and give it to the decimal places asked.

subtopics.title: Liquids when the prescription is in g or micrograms and the label in mg
subtopics.blurb: Convert a g or microgram prescription to match a mg label, then calculate the liquid volume without a thousandfold error.

subtopics.title: Checking a dose against a stated maximum or dose range
subtopics.blurb: Compare a prescribed dose or daily total with a stated maximum or range, and work out what can still safely be given.

subtopics.title: Volume to draw up from an ampoule (mg in 1 mL, mg in 2 mL)
subtopics.blurb: Read an ampoule label correctly and calculate the volume to draw up, whether the strength is per 1 mL, per 2 mL or in micrograms.

subtopics.title: Doses in units: insulin U100, heparin, enoxaparin and nystatin
subtopics.blurb: Handle doses written in units: convert units to mL from the label, and keep units and mL apart.

subtopics.title: Reconstitution, displacement and final concentration
subtopics.blurb: Add the powder's displacement to the diluent, find the final concentration, then draw up the right volume.

subtopics.title: Emergency volumes: IM adrenaline 1 mg/mL by age band, buccal and IV anticonvulsants
subtopics.blurb: Turn adrenaline micrograms into mL from a 1 mg/mL ampoule, and calculate buccal and intravenous anticonvulsant volumes from the strength given.

subtopics.title: Midwifery injections: oxytocin units, vitamin K for the newborn, pethidine
subtopics.blurb: Calculate oxytocin, vitamin K, pethidine and magnesium sulfate injection volumes from the label, including tiny newborn volumes.

subtopics.title: Pump rate in mL per hour from a prescription chart
subtopics.blurb: Read a prescription chart row and set an infusion pump in mL per hour, including infusions over minutes.

subtopics.title: Pump rates that need rounding to the nearest whole number
subtopics.blurb: Round pump rates correctly: half-up, at the very end, to exactly the places the stem asks for.

subtopics.title: Gravity drip rates in drops per minute (drop factor 20, 15 or 60)
subtopics.blurb: Calculate a gravity drip rate in drops per minute using the drop factor given, with time in minutes.

subtopics.title: Infusion duration, volume infused so far and finish time
subtopics.blurb: Work out how long an infusion will take, when it will finish, and how much has gone in or is left.

subtopics.title: Children's and neonatal maintenance fluids (Holliday-Segar, mL/kg/day)
subtopics.blurb: Calculate a child's 24-hour maintenance fluid with the Holliday-Segar bands, a newborn's mL/kg/day volume, and the hourly pump rate.

subtopics.title: Midwifery infusions: oxytocin, magnesium sulfate and the 80 mL/h limit
subtopics.blurb: Set pump rates for magnesium sulfate and oxytocin, and work within the 80 mL/hour fluid limit in severe pre-eclampsia.

subtopics.title: Completing a 24-hour fluid balance chart: total input and total output
subtopics.blurb: Total every input and output column on a 24-hour chart and calculate the balance without dropping an entry.

subtopics.title: Positive and negative balance: the + and - sign in the answer
subtopics.blurb: Decide whether a fluid balance is a gain or a loss and type it with the right sign and unit.

subtopics.title: Counting IV hours at mL/hour on a chart
subtopics.blurb: Count hourly IV entries on a fluid chart correctly, including rate changes and midnight, and turn them into mL.

subtopics.title: Urine output per kg per hour and hourly totals
subtopics.blurb: Work out average hourly urine output and mL/kg/hour for adults, children and babies, and compare it with a threshold given in the stem.

subtopics.title: Feeds and flushes: neonatal mL/kg/day per feed, PEG feeds and water flushes
subtopics.blurb: Work out a baby's volume per feed from mL/kg/day, and total PEG feeds and water flushes on a fluid chart.

subtopics.title: Percentage weight change: newborn weight loss and adult weight loss
subtopics.blurb: Calculate percentage weight loss or gain and new weights for babies, children and adults.

subtopics.title: Pearson answer format: number-only boxes, typed units, no trailing zeros, leading zeros
subtopics.blurb: Type every Part A answer in the exact format Pearson marks correct, in both number-only and typed-unit boxes.

subtopics.title: Rounding to the instruction: decimal places, whole numbers, rounding up ampoules
subtopics.blurb: Round only the final answer, half-up, to exactly the places the stem asks for, and round ampoules up.

subtopics.title: Using the on-screen calculator and the note board
subtopics.blurb: Key Part A calculations on a Standard calculator in a safe order, using the note board to hold the formula and full values.

subtopics.title: Sense-checking answers: estimate first, plausible tablets, volumes and rates
subtopics.blurb: Estimate every answer before calculating and spot tenfold, unit and upside-down errors before you type.

subtopics.title: Pacing at 2 minutes per item and reviewing your answers
subtopics.blurb: Pace Part A at no more than 2 minutes per item, answer every item, and use spare minutes to check format.
